description:
## Goal

Add `callable_identity` as the fourth dimension of the existing atomic `InputDemand` fact. Preserve a callable brand in an activation key exactly when a reachable entry can call it or bake it into a reachable closure; erase identity that is merely transported.

This is not a new fact, cone, solver, or body-wide flag.

## Current defect

`BodyKeying::consumes_callable_identity` is one Boolean for a whole body. Any capture parameter, `ClosureCall`, or `Lambda` in any entry makes every callable input identity-sensitive, including inputs used only by an unreachable arm. `List.reduce/3` consequently keeps distinct outer activations for same-surface reducers on its `{:cont, ...}` path even though the common downstream continuation already owns the indirect call.

The opposite error is also possible: a callable passed through reconstruction or projection can reach an identity consumer through an edge the former forwarding cone did not represent. `fz-kdt.214` therefore supplies the exact typed path relation, and `fz-kdt.213` supplies the one reactive atomic `InputDemand` authority before this dimension lands.

## Correct model

- Derive callable consumption per source input path and reachable entry from lowered SSA provenance.
- Trace closure-call callees and constructed-lambda captures through the shared typed path relation.
- Join the result into `InputDemand { local_dispatch, forwarded_dispatch, returned, callable_identity }` in one publication.
- Dispatch-tested paths remain precise; only ignored transported paths may erase brands.
- Ambiguous reachability conservatively preserves every identity a possible entry can consume.
- Recursive convergence and the existing returned/dispatch decisions remain unchanged.

## Red-first proof

- Two same-surface reducers passed only through `List.reduce/3`'s `{:cont, ...}` arm share one outer activation and remain correct on interp/JIT/AOT.
- `{:suspend, ...}`, a direct closure call, and a lambda capture retain every required construction, layout, and direct target distinction.
- A lambda capturing only data does not make an unrelated callable input identity-sensitive.
- Reconstructed, projected, and protocol-forwarded callables retain identity exactly when the reached consumer uses it.
- Corpus movement has no unexplained executable, dispatch, allocation, ABI/layout, or native-byte change.

## Required deletion and acceptance

Delete `BodyKeying::consumes_callable_identity`, its body-wide scan, stale docs/tests, and every parallel identity-demand path. `DispatchMask` remains the dispatch-question projection; callable identity remains one additional `InputDemand` dimension. Full focused keying/transport/native tests, library, serial matrix, three target doors, cross-process determinism, formatting, check, strict clippy, and docs pass.

comments.text: FOLDED IN from fz-kdt.189 (2026-09-03, filed from the fz-kdt.183 research before this ticket was checked -- it is this ticket's recursive-key half). Facts: (1) Types::convergence_class_at (types/mod.rs:792-796) turns a pure callable slot of a RECURSIVE key into address_var(path): List.reduce_step/3 keys its reducer as a2 while reduce_cont/3's body CALLS it, so the return depends on a slot the key erased. (2) Keeping the callable verbatim (candidate A) measured 7 fixtures hitting the multi-target-closure arg-floor family pinned at drive_test.rs:16351-16394 ("backend dispatch call requires semantic argument N value N: backend value N is unbound" on 00231, 00281, 00285, enum_map_family, enum_reduce_halt_arm_order, opaque_fn_value_join, range_enumerable): a reducer that is a runtime union of targets, specialized per target, stops being materialized (param_reprs [ValueRef, RawInt, RawInt] -> [RawInt, RawInt]) -- the callable half is blocked behind RUNTIME DEMAND, and that pin says the family was fixed; it recurs when a key names a union of targets. (3) On the non-recursive branch erase_closure_identity (types/mod.rs:2926) recurses into captures (:2941): on 00420 Enum.reduce_while/3 (mask all Ignore) collapses seven distinct lambdas into one key `(a2_p0, a2_p1) -> a2_r#?closure[(a1_p0) -> a1_r]`, seven publishers, one return. After fz-kdt.183's element rule 78 blind-shared activations remain, 32 of them Enum.reduce_while/3. (4) body_consumes_callable_identity is one Boolean per body -- exactly this ticket's "current proof"; the transitive form (a forwarder that hands its reducer to a body that calls it consumes identity) is the StaticCallees walk derive_call_graph_component already does. fz-kdt.183 (list element through forwarding) and this ticket (callable identity through reachable entries) are ONE derivation; sequence this after 183 on the same machinery.

GATES MOVED HERE from fz-kdt.183 (its rule review, 2026-09-03): review-attacks b1n.fz, b2n.fz and b4_three_same_driver.fz (identical driver [int], identical seed [], different lambdas) panic at artifact.rs:154 at HEAD and under 183's rule alike -- the minimal pair (kdt122 with different drivers is cured by 183; b1n is not) proves no ELEMENT rule can separate them: only the callable slot the key erases to a2 differs. They are this ticket's red-first gates. Also from that review: the composition is InputDemand { local_dispatch, forwarded_dispatch, identity } on 183's one cone walk -- the dispatch axis itself needs local (what brand erasure and clause reachability read) and forwarded (what the recursive collapse reads) halves; 183 publishes the local half as a co-value and renames the fact.

fz-kdt.183 landed (2e0bb2706). FactKey::InputDemand carries { local_dispatch, forwarded_dispatch }; the identity axis you need is a THIRD component on the SAME cone walk -- collect_demand_cone / ForwardEdge / solve_forwarded_demand in jobs/keying.rs are reusable verbatim, only the per-node LOCAL component differs (ClosureCall callee / Lambda captures traced to clause.params[i]). erase_transported_closure_identities reads local_dispatch explicitly (world.rs; the fz-6gb coupling); when the identity axis exists that read moves to it. b1n/b2n/b4 (independent same-driver reducers) still panic at HEAD and are yours: the minimal pair holds (the two-user Enum.reduce/3 pair is cured, b1n is not).

title: Add callable-identity as the fourth InputDemand dimension
